item.title: Strategy R1: Day and Night
item.description: NVDA by night, AAPL by day. Two auction orders on each side of the session: buy NVDA at the close and hold it overnight, swap it for AAPL at the open, sell AAPL at the close. Two gated energy legs and an FTNT gap-down overlay sit beside it.

item.title: Strategy CF: Barbell: Shaanxi Coal and the Nasdaq-100
item.description: A barbell: a coal stock on one end, the Nasdaq-100 on the other. The two tend to peak at different times. One rule in force nudges the coal position inside a ±10% band. On paper, a three-zone version sets the pair at 90/10, 60/40 or 30/70 by the rank, and two more legs sit on top: a margin add to the Nasdaq-100 when VIX closes above 30, and a one-day buy when the ETF gaps down 3%.

item.title: Factor F1: Off-peak rank, daily
item.description: The reading behind the CF rules: Shaanxi Coal's 42-day return against the Nasdaq-100, ranked in its own two-year range. Updated with each close, with the last twenty days listed one by one.

item.title: Factor F2: Oil volatility (OVX), daily
item.description: The Cboe crude oil volatility index, read against a single line at 50. A close that drops below 50 switches on the R1 USO leg for 21 trading days.

item.title: Factor F3: VIX, daily
item.description: The Cboe volatility index, read against one line at 30. Above it the account treats the tape as an alarm; below it the R1 dip leg is allowed to fire.

item.title: Factor F4: Top-warning lights, live
item.description: Five of the six lights in the account's top-warning rule, measured while the market trades. When three or more are on at once, the rule says risk comes down. Refreshed every 15 minutes during US trading hours.

item.title: Factor F5: Turbulence gauge
item.description: How rough the next three months of the Nasdaq-100 are likely to be. It does not call direction or tops: it reads the Nasdaq volatility index and five lights, and puts the market in one of four tiers.

item.title: What Happened in 2021
item.description: Before 2021, a fall in Chinese home prices was usually temporary. Across the 70 cities in the official price survey, when a city's second-hand prices had fallen over the previous 12 months, they rose over the next 12 months 71% of the time in 2011–2020. Since 2021, that has happened 1% of the time. This note shows where the break happened, what it does to the signals people use to call a bottom, and where the 2026 rebound in Shanghai stands.

item.title: The Market Prices a 5% Chance of $140 Oil. We Think That Is Too Low.
item.description: WTI settled at $103.44 on October 23. After inflation, $140 oil is roughly where the market spent much of 2011–14, not a fantasy number. The spare capacity that capped earlier spikes is thinner than it was before the war, and inventories are falling. The futures curve still says $81 a year from now. This note sets out why we think the upside tail is underpriced, what the market itself is pricing, the evidence that cuts against us, and what would prove us wrong.
